title_seen: Time-Predictable Acceleration of Deep Neural Networks on FPGA SoCs with Multi-Core DPUs
work_done: Scheduling and analysis framework for multi-core AMD DPU configurations on FPGA SoCs: AXI bus budgeting units regulate per-core memory traffic, DNNs are split into chunks, and limited-preemptive fixed-priority scheduling gets a response-time analysis.
advantages: Gives response-time guarantees for concurrent DNN tasks on a commercial Zynq UltraScale+ platform, and reports large schedulability gains over the standard Vitis AI setup across all evaluated scenarios.
disadvantages: Chunk WCETs come from profiling (10,000 inferences under memory interference), not from an analytical model. The DPU is a closed black box; evaluated on ZCU102 with DPUs at 90 MHz; CPU pre/post-processing is left to future work.
relevance: Closest prior on time-predictable DNN inference on Zynq US+; contrast: measured-WCET bound on a black-box DPU vs V3's exact compile-time cycle count on custom RTL.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I-II, V, VII-A (setup, profiling), VIII related work, IX conclusions

title_seen: Time-Predictable Acceleration of Deep Neural Networks on FPGA SoC Platforms
work_done: Profiles the Xilinx DPU on Zynq UltraScale+ (ZCU102) with a custom AXI bus profiler, derives a series-parallel execution model and response-time analysis, and adds DICTAT, an FPGA module that fetches DPU instructions from on-chip memory.
advantages: Safe analytical upper bounds for DPU inference of ADAS DNNs, validated against on-board measurements; DICTAT reduces bound pessimism by at least 12% overall (25% for pedestrian detection).
disadvantages: Bounds, not exact predictions: measured latency still varies (e.g. Lane Detect 7.09-7.12 ms over 1000 runs, attributed to DRAM). Single black-box DPU, model built from profiling.
relevance: Baseline line of work for time-predictable DNN acceleration on the same SoC family as the KV260; V3 contrasts exact cycle equality with RTA bounds.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I-III (profiling, Tables I-II), VII (Table III), conclusions

title_seen: DERCA: DetERministic Cycle-Level Accelerator on Reconfigurable Platforms in DNN-Enabled Real-Time Safety-Critical Systems
work_done: Accelerator architecture with fine-grained intra-layer preemption and cycle-level determinism, an on-chip EDF scheduler and a dataflow with intra-layer preemption points; predictability analysis under the limited-preemptive task model enables schedulability analysis and preemption-point placement.
advantages: Reduces priority inversion versus non-preemptive and layer-wise preemptive dataflows with under 5% WCET overhead and 6% extra resources on AMD VCK190; open-sourced.
disadvantages: Evaluated on Versal ACAP (VCK190), not Zynq UltraScale+. Full text not yet public (NSF PAR embargo to 2026-12-02), so how WCET is derived and whether model and board cycles are compared was not checked.
relevance: Closest custom-accelerator prior claiming cycle-level determinism; V3 must position its exact model=RTL=board equality against it. Read full text when available.

work_done: Proposes STT-VTA, a superscalar extension of the time-triggered VTA: pattern-based timing schedules from an extended simulator plus a configuration manager decide how many extra VTA modules a model needs.
advantages: Keeps deterministic temporal use of shared memories and buses (time-triggered) while cutting inference time by 20-41% versus a single (TT-)VTA, with identical classification accuracy.
disadvantages: Evaluation as described in the abstract uses a software simulator (DRAMSim2 for memory instructions plus a cycle-accurate simulator); no board measurement is mentioned there. The earlier TT-VTA was slower on average (53 vs 51 ms).
relevance: Closest time-triggered custom DNN accelerator line; contrast with V3's on-board cycle-exact verification.

title_seen: ART: Customizing Accelerators for DNN-Enabled Real-Time Safety-Critical Systems
work_done: HW/SW co-design framework that turns HLS-based FPGA DNN accelerators into real-time ones: schedulability analysis and preemption-point placement in software, and hardware GEDF scheduling with save/resume preemption via source-code transformation.
advantages: Meets schedulability where baseline accelerators miss deadlines on AMD VCK190; scheduler hardware takes a fixed small number of cycles and uses <0.5% resources; about 100 lines of user input generate about 2.5k lines of code.
disadvantages: Task WCETs are inputs to the analysis; we found no statement on how they are derived in the sections read. Evaluated on Versal VCK190 with two baseline accelerator models; one accelerator shared by all tasks (heterogeneous/partial reconfiguration future work).
relevance: Real-time scheduling of FPGA DNN accelerators; V3 provides the exact per-layer WCETs such frameworks assume.
notes: Crossref match. Predecessor of ji2025derca (same group).

title_seen: Vicuna: A Timing-Predictable RISC-V Vector Coprocessor for Scalable Parallel Computation
work_done: Timing-anomaly-free RISC-V vector coprocessor integrated with Ibex (128 8-bit MACs/cycle, 80 MHz on Xilinx 7-series), evaluated on data-parallel benchmarks including 3x3 convolution and matrix multiplication.
advantages: Each benchmark always runs in exactly the same number of cycles, and repeated runs with varying inputs give identical times; over 90% efficiency on compute-bound tasks while enabling compositional WCET analysis.
disadvantages: Performance figures come from measurement, not timing analysis (Sec. 5). It is a programmable processor, not a CNN accelerator, and is evaluated on kernels rather than full networks.
relevance: Prior evidence of run-to-run cycle constancy on FPGA; V3 adds analytical prediction equal to the measurement for full CNNs.

title_seen: Work-in-Progress: Real-Time Neural Network Inference on a Custom RISC-V Multicore Vector Processor
work_done: Multicore architecture of predictable Ibex+Vicuna vector cores with local scratchpads and a management core; an MLIR compiler splits int8 NNs into subtasks and computes a static compile-time schedule for shared-memory transfers from subtask WCET estimates.
advantages: Removes memory-subsystem interference by construction through a precomputed transfer schedule, giving a composable WCET for NN inference; SystemVerilog design targeting UltraScale+ FPGAs.
disadvantages: Work-in-progress: FPGA evaluation is future work and the compiler-based scheduling and deployment are stated as ongoing work; no measured results.
relevance: Compile-time static scheduling for predictable NN inference; processor-based contrast to V3's fixed-function array.
notes: Crossref match. Follow-up kirschner2026multivic (VCU128 measurements, non-zero fluctuation) considered as spare.

title_seen: ACETONE: Predictable Programming Framework for ML Applications in Safety-Critical Systems
work_done: Generates semantics-preserving, traceable C code from trained feed-forward DNNs so that the WCET can be computed with the OTAWA static analyser; compared with Keras2c and uTVM on a set of benchmarks.
advantages: Targets avionics certification needs (traceability, WCET computation); static WCET bounds from OTAWA plus measured times on Cortex-A15; artifact-evaluated.
disadvantages: Software/CPU only, no accelerator. WCET computed for an lpc2138 ARM target chosen for OTAWA support, which the authors note is not representative of the Cortex-A15 used for measurements.
relevance: Software WCET line for DNN inference; contrast with hardware whose latency is exact rather than statically bounded.

title_seen: PREMA: A Predictive Multi-Task Scheduling Algorithm For Preemptible Neural Processing Units
work_done: Proposes preemption mechanisms for a TPU-like NPU and a predictive multi-task scheduler that uses a job-size prediction model, relying on the deterministic compute and memory behaviour of DNNs on the NPU.
advantages: Preemptive NPU multi-tasking gives average 7.8x latency, 1.4x throughput and 4.8x SLA-satisfaction improvements; shows that NPU execution time is predictable enough to schedule on.
disadvantages: Cloud/datacenter throughput-and-SLA focus, not hard real-time guarantees. Evaluation uses a cycle-level performance model with fixed memory bandwidth and latency (simulation, no hardware).
relevance: Classic accelerator-level preemptive scheduling exploiting DNN latency predictability; motivates exact latency as a scheduler input.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. II-III (NPU model, methodology)

title_seen: AXI HyperConnect: A Predictable, Hypervisor-level Interconnect for Hardware Accelerators in FPGA SoC
work_done: Hypervisor-level hardware interconnect that lets FPGA accelerators from different criticality domains share a memory bus while ensuring isolation and predictability, implemented on Xilinx FPGA SoCs.
advantages: Addresses interference between PL accelerators on a shared AXI bus; tested with real-world accelerators including a DNN inference accelerator.
disadvantages: Abstract only read; it gives no quantitative results. Concerns isolation of the shared bus, not the internal timing of the accelerator.
relevance: Predictable interconnect for PL accelerators on Zynq SoCs; relevant if V3 shares DRAM/AXI with other masters (exactness scope beyond on-chip compute).
